title: Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020
short_title: Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The government introduced the Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020 to support a $13.5 million pilot of family safety risk screening and triage processes in the Brisbane, Parramatta and Adelaide family law court registries, including a specialist Evatt List for high-risk matters, with confidentiality and immunity protections for court officials.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020 should be passed to support the Lighthouse Project, a domestic violence risk‑screening pilot trialled in Adelaide, Brisbane and Parramatta, and criticised the Morrison government for delaying the legislation while calling for additional funding for frontline family violence services.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wallace
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020, which makes risk-screening information inadmissible in legal proceedings except to protect children or prevent serious harm, enabling the $13.5 million Lighthouse Project pilot in Adelaide, Brisbane and Parramatta. The speech also cited $490 million in government funding for domestic violence measures, including $2.6 million for Coast2Bay emergency accommodation on the Sunshine Coast.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Family Law Amendment (Risk Screening Protections) Bill 2020 as a necessary step but criticised the government for years of delay and insufficient funding, noting that domestic violence is a factor in 79% of Legal Aid family law matters and that 8.2% of women experienced first-time physical violence during COVID-19. They also argued for removing the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility in custody cases and for increased resourcing of courts, legal services, and community organisations.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The bill supports the government-funded Lighthouse Project, piloted in the Adelaide, Brisbane and Parramatta federal family law court registries from 2020 to mid-2022 with $13.5 million in funding, by making risk screening information confidential and inadmissible with limited child-safety exceptions and granting court workers immunity. The government has invested over $1 billion in addressing family violence since 2013.
